text:
janet: Quick update from People Ops  We're kicking off a 6-month pilot next Monday for a Backup Care Stipend + Emergency Travel Advance to help when last-minute caregiving needs pop up. Short summary + how to request below.

janet: Pilot highlights: 
- $1,000 one-time backup care stipend (can be used for in-home care, daycare drop-in, or adult/elder care services).
- Emergency Travel Advance: up to $1,500 for last-minute round-trip travel if you need to return home for urgent caregiving. Advances are repayable from your next payroll but can be waived in hardship cases.
- Global coverage varies; local law and payroll rules may affect advances. See the policy link. :earth_africa:

omar: does the stipend stack with PTO or is it separate?

janet: Good Q. It's separate from PTO and is intended to cover care services costs so you can remain working or take short blocks of time off. It does not convert to extra days off.

kelly: timeline/process for the advance? sometimes I need cash day-of.

janet: We have two routes:
1) Advance request (recommended): submit the Emergency Travel Advance form and People Ops & Payroll aim to approve and disburse within 2 business days.
2) Retro reimburse (if you paid out-of-pocket): submit receipts + short note within 7 business days; reimbursement target is 4 business days.
If you truly need same-day funds, talk to your manager and tag @people-ops-urgent in the form; we will prioritize on a case-by-case basis.

ryan: who qualifies for backup care stipend? my partners elderly parent needs sporadic help.

janet: Eligible uses: dependent children, immediate family members (parents, partners), and legal dependents living in your household or dependent on you for care. Exceptional out-of-house dependents may be approved with brief justification. Local HR will confirm edge cases.

emily: payroll question  will the advance show as taxable income?

janet: The stipend is not payroll income; it's a reimbursement/stipend (non-cash benefit) in most regions. Advances are payroll disbursements and may appear on pay statements; tax treatment depends on local jurisdiction. Payroll will include a note when they process.

people-ops-bot: Policy draft uploaded: https://redwoodinference.internal/people-ops/policies/backup-care-emergency-travel-2026-draft.pdf - includes country-specific notes and manager guidance. :link:

kelly: would be great to have a manager quick-guide and a one-click checkbox in the time-off form for backup-care so managers see it.

janet: Agreed. We're creating a 1-page manager playbook and asked DevEx to add a form checkbox during the pilot (ticket created). Adding @ryan to help with the manager communications.

ryan: will do. also suggest a short template managers can use when approving travel advances so Finance has the right context.

janet: We'll attach a sample approval template in the policy doc.

omar: reporting  will People Ops share uptake metrics? curious how this affects remote teams and regional differences.

janet: Yes  we'll publish anonymized monthly metrics to the People Ops channel and a mid-pilot summary for leadership. Metrics: number of stipends used, advances disbursed, average time to reimburse, and top use-cases by region.

emily: any change for contractors?

janet: Not part of the stipend pilot. Contractors should speak to their managers; Finance may be able to support ad-hoc.

kelly: thanks  this is big for working parents. quick ask: can we include sample receipts that qualify (e.g., in-home caregiver invoice, daycare drop-in)?

janet: Yep  sample receipts and acceptable justification snippets are in the policy doc. We want the process to be low friction.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: pilot starts 2026-05-04. Midpoint review scheduled 2026-07-06 at 10am PT (calendar invite will be posted).

janet: Thanks team. If you have edge cases DM me or drop questions here. We'll post an all-hands blurb and update the handbook once legal signs off on the final doc.
